title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 63 (Promisee may dispense with or remit performance of promise)

content.overview: Section 63 provides that every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.
content.glance: Promisee may dispense with or remit performance (wholly/partly), extend time, or accept any satisfaction in lieu — without fresh consideration.
content.study: The promisee may dispense with or remit performance wholly or in part, extend the time for performance, or accept any satisfaction instead of the original performance. Under Indian law this does not require fresh consideration. Current-law framing: identify dispensation, remission, extension of time, or acceptance of alternative satisfaction by the promisee; conclude the promisor is relieved to that extent.

sections.heading: Dispense or remit
sections.body: Promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise.

sections.heading: Extend time
sections.body: Promisee may extend the time for such performance.

sections.heading: Accept satisfaction
sections.body: Promisee may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.

provisions.title: Promisee may dispense with or remit performance of promise

examples.title: Remission of part
examples.body: A owes B ₹5,000. B accepts ₹2,000 in full satisfaction. The remainder is remitted under s. 63.

hypotheticals.question: Is fresh consideration required for remission under s. 63?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 63 allows the promisee to remit or accept satisfaction without the need for fresh consideration under the Act.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-63
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Remission of part of a debt always requires fresh consideration as in English common law.
misconceptions.correction: Section 63 permits the promisee to remit or accept any satisfaction without requiring fresh consideration.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 63 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify dispensation, remission, extension or alternative satisfaction. II. Apply relief of the promisor to that extent. III. Conclude.

examTips: Stress no need for fresh consideration under s. 63.
List the three powers of the promisee.
